name: TOM
description: Lena's younger brother who works at the ferry ticket office. He assists with managing his father's medical supplies and helps secure the office during night operations.

explicit_evidence.quote: TOM, her younger brother, sets a blue insulated medicine case on the counter.

explicit_evidence.trait: Responsible for father's medical care coordination
explicit_evidence.quote: Dad's doses. The clinic launch comes at six. Don't leave this in the locker.

explicit_evidence.trait: Follows instructions and defers to sister's authority
explicit_evidence.quote: Tom reaches for the case, but Lena stops him.
The office is locked. Someone left an orange cape on the bench outside.
Was that Dad in the photograph?

inferred_traits.rationale: Tom brings his father's medical doses to the office and follows his sister's instructions without question, suggesting familial responsibility and obedience.
Tom notices and reports the abandoned orange cape left on the bench, demonstrating attention to detail and awareness of his surroundings.
Tom defers to Lena's decisions throughout the scenes, accepting her instructions without resistance or argument.
Tom's question about whether their father appears in a photograph suggests emotional investment in family matters.

dialogue_summary: Tom delivers his father's medical doses to the ticket office and instructs his sister not to leave them in the locker. Later, he calls from the office to report an abandoned orange cape. Finally, he asks Lena whether their father appeared in a photograph.

relationships.evidence: Tom is Lena's younger brother; he defers to her authority and follows her instructions throughout the scenes.
Tom brings his father's medical doses and is concerned about his father's whereabouts and appearance in a photograph.
Tom communicates with Ruth indirectly through Lena; they work in the same operational context (ferry/clinic launch system).
